title: MedMNIST v2 - A Large-Scale Lightweight Benchmark for 2D and 3D Biomedical Image Classification
authors: Jiancheng Yang, Rui Shi, Donglai Wei, Zequan Liu, Lin Zhao, Bilian Ke, Hanspeter Pfister, Bingbing Ni
conclusions: Introduces MedMNIST v2, a standardized MNIST-like collection of 12 2D + 6 3D biomedical image classification datasets (708,069 2D images, 9,998 3D images), all preprocessed to 28x28 (2D) or 28x28x28 (3D) with official train/val/test splits.

TissueMNIST (kidney cortex cells, BBBC051, 8 classes, 236,386 images), DermMNIST (HAM10000 dermatoscopic images, 7 classes, 10,015 images), and OCTMNIST (retinal OCT, 4 classes, 109,309 images) are among the 12 2D sub-datasets, each with documented source, task type, class count, and split sizes.
Benchmarks several baseline methods (ResNet-18/50 at two resolutions, auto-sklearn, AutoKeras, Google AutoML Vision) on every sub-dataset using AUC and ACC, repeated >=3 trials per method.

Positions MedMNIST v2 as a lightweight, diverse, standardized, educational 'decathlon' benchmark for biomedical image analysis, intended to ease entry for non-domain researchers and enable fair algorithm comparison.
Explicitly states the resized 28x28 data is NOT intended for clinical use and recommends citing both the original source dataset paper (e.g., HAM10000) and MedMNIST v1/v2.
Data, code, and evaluation scripts are publicly released (medmnist.com, GitHub).
